ruby.source: .ruby-version, Dockerfile.base / Dockerfile.development / Dockerfile.production FROM ruby:4.0.9-slim-trixie (Phase 18; Phase 13 moved 3.1.7 → 3.4.12, Phase 14 Bookworm → Trixie)
ruby.notes: 4.0.9 is the newest 4.0 release on 2026-10-25 (ruby 4.0.9 (2026-10-23 revision 3e93b23afc) +PRISM; +YJIT once Rails' config.yjit turns it on) and the newest ruby:4.0.x-slim-trixie tag (fetch_latest_versions.py docker_tags). Ruby 4.0 stable patches ship every two months, so the FROM lines pin the full patch. The image ships RubyGems 4.0.20, Bundler 4.0.20, Debian 13.7, and these default gems: erb 6.0.7 (why the lock moved erb — see bundler.notes), psych 5.3.1, json 2.18.0, io-console 0.8.2, prism 1.8.2, stringio 3.2.0, tsort 0.2.0, date 3.5.1; bundled gems: minitest 6.0.0 (lock keeps 5.27.0), reline 0.6.3 (lock 0.7.0 — the `ambiguous specs: reline` WARN once per rspec boot), rdoc 7.0.4 (lock 8.1.0 — the two rubygems plugins make the `gem` CLI print eight `already initialized constant RDoc::*` warnings; rspec/rails are silent), irb 1.16.0, csv 3.3.5, bigdecimal 4.0.1 (lock 3.3.1), base64 0.3.0, drb 2.2.3, ostruct 0.6.3, logger 1.7.0, benchmark 0.5.0, pstore 0.2.1, racc 1.8.1, debug 1.11.1. Pathname and Set are core classes (the `require 'pathname'` lines in bin/setup and bin/update became RuboCop Lint/RedundantRequireStatement offences under TargetRubyVersion 4.0 and were removed); the CGI library is gone except cgi/escape (erb 6 no longer depends on the cgi gem, which left the lock). Other lines on 2026-10-25: 3.4.12 (EOL 2028-03-31, what Phases 13–17 ran), 3.3.13 (security-only, EOL 2027-03-31); 3.2 went EOL 2026-03-31. 4.1 (2026-12-25) makes tsort a bundled gem — rails 8.1.4 emitted no tsort warning under -W:deprecated here.

bundler.source: Gemfile.lock BUNDLED WITH, Dockerfiles gem install bundler -v 4.0.20; Phase 18
bundler.notes: The Bundler ruby:4.0.9-slim-trixie ships as its default gem (RubyGems 4.0.20); 4.0.23 (2026-10-14) is the newest 4.0.x on rubygems.org but, as in Phase 13, the repo pins what the image ships rather than installing a newer one on top. Observed on the upgraded lockfile: `bundle lock` rewrote only BUNDLED WITH (2.6.9 → 4.0.20, indented two spaces instead of three), added NO CHECKSUMS section (only new lockfiles or `bundle lock --add-checksums` get one), and kept PLATFORMS aarch64-linux / ruby / x86_64-linux. Bundler 4 removed `bundle install --frozen` (exit 15: 'The --frozen flag has been removed because it relied on being remembered across bundler invocations'); Dockerfile.ci and Dockerfile.production now run `BUNDLE_FROZEN=true bundle install`, which still refuses a Gemfile that disagrees with the lock (exit 16, lock untouched). The Gemfile's `:mingw` / `:x64_mingw` platform symbols are deprecated in favour of `:windows` (byebug line changed; no warning printed). Bundler also auto-unlocks a default gem whose locked version is older than the one Ruby already activated: erb 4.0.4.1 raised `Gem::LoadError: You have already activated erb 6.0.7` at Bundler.setup, fixed with `bundle lock --update erb --conservative`.
